cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.summary: Christ, with a cross-nimbus and holding a book, sits in a green mandorla between two angels, while tongues of flame burst up on either side and consume a fallen enemy at the lower left. The psalm proclaims 'The Lord reigneth … a fire goeth before him, and burneth up his enemies round about'.
facts: The Stuttgart Psalter was made around 820–830 at the abbey of Saint-Germain-des-Prés near Paris; its 168 leaves contain the psalms with 316 coloured miniatures set between the verses they illustrate.
Its pictures interpret the psalms literally, historically or — very often — Christologically, as prophecies of the life of Christ.
cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.notes: Image from the WLB digital facsimile (Public Domain Mark), showing the whole page with the miniature.

cur:manuscripts2-utrecht-canticle-benedi.summary: A half-figure of the cross-nimbed Christ-Logos holding a book appears in a mandorla in the centre of the heavens, surrounded by the works of creation called upon to bless him in the Benedicite: sun and moon, winds, angels with bannered staffs, showers and dew, birds in the trees, the children of men, beasts of every kind, and whales and all that move in the waters. It is one of the most cosmic drawings in the book.
facts: The Utrecht Psalter illustrates every psalm and canticle with a lively pen drawing — 166 in all — that translates the words of the text, often literally, into images; in these the Lord of the psalms is regularly shown as the youthful Christ-Logos.
After centuries in England the manuscript arrived in Utrecht in 1716; it is often called the most valuable manuscript in the Netherlands.
cur:manuscripts2-utrecht-canticle-benedi.notes: The figure of the Lord is identified as Christ (the Christ-Logos) following the commentary of the Utrecht University Library's annotated edition, which describes the psalter's consistent practice of drawing the God of the psalms as the youthful Christ. The image is a crop of the drawing from the library's IIIF image server.
